hook: This file carries an adult-content warning, and much of the worst material is redacted anyway. Behind the clinical opening is a field report in the voice of a badly shaken team leader, and that voice is the reason to read it. Expect crude language and a deeply unpleasant setting.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of an article that changes register mid-document, from detached procedures to a raw, profane first-person account. The collision between a formal report and a writer who clearly cannot keep it formal is its main craft point. The closing notice and the link to a revised report also show how a story on the site can spill across pages.
thingsToNotice:
The after-action report starts in proper military style and falls apart within a few lines, and the writer even asks a colleague to tidy it up later. Framing it as a first draft gives the article permission to be rough.

Pay attention to the lieutenant and the young corporal: the older man keeps managing the rookie's fear, and at the crucial moment the roles flip. The arithmetic about air and suit power gives a grim, practical edge to an absurd situation. Dark humor and real grief sit side by side, and the expunged passages leave the bleakest parts for the linked follow-up.

related.note: Another vast ocean organism approached through crewed dives.
Another account told in the shaken voice of someone who went inside.
